title: 9-round AES-256: related-key partial sums, data conflict for selected subkey recovery

target.description: AES-256 reduced to 9 rounds on 128-bit blocks; initial AddRoundKey k^(0), then rounds 1 through 9, with no MixColumns in the final round. The improved filter guesses 19 bytes of expanded-key cycle K^(4), tracks the key-dependent differences, then applies partial sums to the remaining late-round material. This is the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey search.

setting.key_relation: For an unknown base master key L, L_a XOR L has byte a at zero-based master-key byte indices 21 and 25 and zero elsewhere, for every a in 0,...,255. The a=0 key is the base key; total distinct keys is 256.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: About 32 structures, each containing 2^64 chosen plaintexts under each of 256 related master keys. Body total 2^77 conflicts with Table 1's 2^85.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

The paper presents these constructions as attacks on Rijndael. This record prices the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey filter; complete master-key reconstruction and any repeated filter applications are left for a separate completion-budget review.
Related master keys use a fixed XOR relation, while their expanded-key differences depend on guessed base-key bytes through S-boxes. These are not arbitrary independently selectable subkey oracles.

time.note: Section 4.3 gives 5*2^224 for five dominating structures, each scanning 2^72 ciphertexts for 2^152 outer guesses. Section 4.5 abbreviates this to 2^224 steps. The coefficient five is preserved; the dominant one-round-decryption workload is not silently converted to full AES encryptions.

data.note: Both versions print the discrepancy. The body counts 32*(2^64*256)=2^77 total queries; Table 1 states 2^85. The table's extra factor 256 cannot be explained as a per-key/total conversion of the same stated structure count.

memory.note: Neither the basic nor improved related-key construction provides an explicit complete peak-storage budget.

success.description: No numerical success for this exact partial_key_recovery output is given. Section4.2 says enough sets identify the correct guesses; Section4.3 says about32 structures, without a joint error probability. The source 256-key relation and required plaintext compensation are conditions of the balanced identity. The existing Table1 2^85 versus body 2^77 data conflict remains pending; neither endpoint is silently selected.

review.scope: Re-read PDF3-5 and11-16 Sections2.1-2.4/4.1-4.5. The improved related-key procedure intends unique guessed-byte output after about32 structures, but supplies no joint wrong-key law for these aggregate structures or explicit master-key completion for the headline. Earlier ordinary Square255/256 rejection is not that law. Retain partial/full separation, balanced-sum component and2^85-versus2^77 data conflict; both primary metrics remain unquantified.
